funder: European Research Council (ERC) – Starting Grant
eligibility: Any nationality. From the 2027 call: PhD defended 0–10 years before 1 Jan 2027 (previously 2–7 years). Host in an EU Member State or Associated Country; PI spends at least 50% of working time there.
funded: Five-year frontier research project led by the PI: own salary, team, equipment, other direct costs plus 25% overhead. 2027 call closed 14 Oct 2026.
amount: Up to €1.5m for 5 years; plus up to €1m for justified extra costs (equipment, fieldwork, start-up); up to €2m extra for PIs relocating from outside the EU/AC.

funder: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions – Postdoctoral Fellowships
eligibility: Any nationality. PhD at the call deadline and at most 8 years full-time-equivalent research experience after the PhD. Mobility rule: no more than 12 months in the host country in the 3 years before the deadline.
funded: Employment of the fellow at a host organisation: European Fellowships 12–24 months; Global Fellowships 12–24 months abroad plus a 12-month return phase. 2026 call closed 9 Sep 2026; 2027 call planned 7 Apr–8 Sep 2027.
amount: Per month (2026–27 rates): living allowance €6,350 × country coefficient, mobility €710, family €660 if applicable. Host gets €1,000 research/training and €650 management per month.

funder: MSCA – Doctoral Networks
eligibility: For doctoral candidates: you apply to advertised positions (EURAXESS), not to the EU. Candidates must not already hold a doctorate; the MSCA mobility rule applies to the recruiting country.
funded: Doctoral position (employment contract) within an international training network; secondments to other partners.
amount: Per month (2026 call): living allowance €4,250 × country coefficient (e.g. Germany 101.5% ≈ €4,314), mobility €710, family €660 if applicable.

funder: DFG – Emmy Noether Programme
eligibility: All disciplines; normally up to 4 years after the doctorate (6 for licensed applicants in medicine/psychology), normally at least 2 years postdoctoral experience and substantial international research experience. Not for those already habilitated. Applicants from abroad must intend to stay in Germany.
funded: Independent junior research group for 6 years (3 + 3 after evaluation): own position as group leader, staff, project funds, optional modules (family allowance, workshops, etc.). Rolling submission.
amount: No fixed ceiling; budget requested by module and reviewed.

funder: DFG – Walter Benjamin Programme
eligibility: Early postdoctoral phase; generally requires a change of institution. Fellowship abroad only for researchers integrated into the German system (e.g. at least 3 continuous years as researcher in Germany before applying).
funded: Own project for up to 2 years. Abroad: fellowship. In Germany: own position (“postdoctoral researcher and comparable”). Both: allowance for project, travel and publication costs. Rolling submission.
amount: Fellowship = monthly basic amount plus foreign/cost-of-living allowances, travel and child benefits (DFG award calculator); position in Germany paid at DFG personnel rates.

funder: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation – Humboldt Research Fellowship
eligibility: Non-German researchers of any discipline (Germans only if settled abroad >5–10 years). Postdocs: doctorate within the last 4 years; experienced researchers: within 12 years. No more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying. Next call opens 15 Nov 2026 (capped at 800 applications).
funded: Research stay at a German host institution: 6–24 months (postdocs), 6–18 months (experienced). Optional language course, family benefits, travel lump sum.
amount: €3,000/month (postdocs); €3,600/month (experienced). Host receives a research-cost allowance of €500/month (humanities/social sciences) or €800/month (natural sciences/engineering).

funder: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation – Feodor Lynen Research Fellowship
eligibility: German citizens (non-Germans if integrated in German academia and based in Germany). Postdocs: doctorate within the last 4 years (or within 6 months of completion); experienced: within 12 years. Host must be a member of the Humboldt Network abroad.
funded: Research stay abroad: 6–24 months (postdocs), 6–18 months (experienced). Travel costs, family allowances; optional 12-month return fellowship.
amount: Varies by host country and family situation (Humboldt fellowship calculator). Host expected to cover about one third (waived for some countries).

funder: DAAD – Research Grants for doctoral candidates
eligibility: International (non-German) doctoral candidates and early postdocs; calls and conditions differ by country of origin.
funded: Research stays in Germany (one-year grants, short-term grants) or a full doctorate in Germany; health/accident/liability insurance, travel allowance, language course.
amount: €1,300/month for doctoral candidates.

funder: Begabtenförderungswerke (13 federally funded foundations, e.g. Studienstiftung, Friedrich-Ebert-, Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung)
eligibility: Doctoral candidates at German universities with excellent degrees; each foundation adds its own criteria (political, religious or other orientation, social engagement).
funded: Doctoral scholarship, normally 3 years (extensions possible, e.g. with children), plus seminars and networking; family and childcare supplements.
amount: Since 1 Oct 2025: €1,650/month basic scholarship + €100/month research-cost allowance (€1,750).

funder: UKRI doctoral studentships (via Doctoral Training Partnerships / Centres for Doctoral Training)
eligibility: PhD applicants to UKRI-funded programmes at UK universities; apply to the university/DTP, not to UKRI.
funded: Tax-free stipend plus tuition fees (UKRI pays fees at the home rate) and research training support.
amount: From 1 Oct 2026: minimum stipend £21,805/year (£23,805 with London weighting); minimum fee £5,238/year.

funder: ESRC – Postdoctoral Fellowships
eligibility: Social sciences (≥50%). UK PhD from a research organisation in ESRC’s doctoral training network; no more than 15 months of active postdoctoral experience at the closing date (2026 call: 1 Jun 2026). Applied for via a Doctoral Training Partnership.
funded: Up to 9 months full-time (18 months part-time) to consolidate the PhD: publications, networks, career development.
amount: Salary and costs at 80% of full economic cost (host covers the rest).

funder: British Academy – Postdoctoral Fellowships
eligibility: Humanities and social sciences. Viva within 3 years (2026 round: 1 Apr 2024–1 Apr 2027). UK/EEA nationals regardless of where the doctorate was obtained, or any nationality with a UK doctorate. No current/former permanent post. One application per eligibility window. 2026 deadline 30 Sep 2026 (passed).
funded: Three-year fellowship at a UK host; salary and research expenses; limited teaching allowed.
amount: 80% of salary/full economic cost (host covers 20%). Research expenses up to £6,000 over 3 years per the 2026 Oxford/UCL call documents; some 2026 summaries cite £10,000†.

funder: Leverhulme Trust – Early Career Fellowships
eligibility: Within 4 years of the viva (2027 round: viva 18 Feb 2023–18 Feb 2027). UK degree or employment at a UK HEI; no full-time permanent academic post held. Most subjects (some health-related fields excluded). Deadline 18 Feb 2027†; host internal deadlines are earlier.
funded: Three-year research post at a UK university to complete a significant piece of publishable work. Host must offer matched funding.
amount: Trust pays the salary in year 1 up to £56,000 and 50% in years 2–3 (host pays the rest)†; plus up to £6,000/year research expenses.

funder: UKRI – Future Leaders Fellowships
eligibility: Researchers/innovators transitioning to or establishing independence; any nationality; UK host. No fixed years-since-PhD rule. Round 11 academic deadline was 16 Jun 2026†.
funded: Personal fellowship for 4 years, renewable for 3 more: own salary, team, research costs.
amount: UKRI funds 80% of full economic cost; awards have ranged from about £300,000 to over £2m.

funder: National Science Foundation – Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP)
eligibility: U.S. citizens, nationals or permanent residents; final-year undergraduates and early-stage graduate students in NSF-supported fields (incl. economics and other social sciences) at U.S. institutions.
funded: 3 years of support within a 5-year window for a research master’s or PhD.
amount: $37,000/year stipend + $16,000/year cost-of-education allowance to the institution.

funder: National Institutes of Health – Kirschstein NRSA individual fellowships (F31 predoctoral, F32 postdoctoral)
eligibility: Health-related research at NIH institutes; NRSA fellowships are restricted to U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals and permanent residents.
funded: Stipend, tuition/fees and institutional allowance during training under a sponsor.
amount: FY2026 stipends: predoctoral $29,364/year; postdoctoral from $63,480 (0 years’ experience) to $77,076 (7+ years).

funder: Alfred P. Sloan Foundation – Sloan Research Fellowships
eligibility: Tenure-track but untenured faculty with a regular teaching obligation at a U.S. or Canadian institution; fields include economics. Nomination by a senior colleague. 2027 nominations closed 15 Sep 2026.
funded: Flexible research support over 2 years (staff, travel, equipment, summer salary).
amount: $75,000 over 2 years.

funder: NSF – SBE Postdoctoral Research Fellowships (SPRF)
eligibility: Social, behavioural and economic sciences. Currently not accepting proposals: NSF lists the programme as awaiting a new solicitation.
funded: Under the last solicitation (NSF 23-500): up to 24 months of postdoctoral training with a host.
amount: Last solicitation: $65,000/year stipend + $15,000/year research and training allowance ($160,000 total).

funder: Tri-Agency (CIHR, NSERC, SSHRC) – Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D)
eligibility: Doctoral students at Canadian institutions (harmonised programme replacing CGS-D and the agency-specific doctoral awards). Citizenship/residency rules are set per call; check the agency page.
funded: Doctoral scholarship, 36 months.

funder: Tri-Agency – Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA), successor to the Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships
eligibility: Postdocs applying via the agency matching their field. Banting ran its last competition in 2024 and now points to CPRA. 2026 deadlines: SSHRC 10 Sep, CIHR 16 Sep, NSERC 17 Oct (all passed)†. Citizenship rules per agency.
funded: Postdoctoral award for 24 months.
amount: CAD 70,000/year ≈ €44,800/year (€89,500 total), taxable.

funder: Australian Research Council – Discovery Early Career Researcher Award (DECRA)
eligibility: Up to 5 years since the PhD (plus allowable interruptions); application via an eligible Australian organisation; international applicants need the right to work in Australia. Annual round; DE27 ran 28 Jan–11 Mar 2026†.
funded: Three-year fellowship: salary plus on-costs and project funds.
amount: Salary contribution AUD 126,693 incl. on-costs (DE26 rate) ≈ €79,900/year; plus up to AUD 50,000/year project costs ≈ €31,500/year.

funder: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) – Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard)
eligibility: Citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan (not Japanese citizens/permanent residents). Doctorate within 6 years of the fellowship start (FY2027: assessed from 1 Apr 2027). Japanese host required. Also available via national nominating bodies (in Germany: Humboldt Foundation).
funded: 12–24 months of collaborative research in Japan; return airfare, insurance; research grant can be applied for separately.
amount: JPY 362,000/month ≈ €2,060/month; settling-in allowance JPY 200,000 ≈ €1,140.

funder: Dutch Research Council (NWO) – Talent Programme Veni
eligibility: Any nationality; PhD obtained within 3 years before the round’s reference date (2026 round: 1 Jan 2026) or between that date and the deadline. Must carry out the project at a Dutch knowledge institution. 2026 pre-proposal deadline 1 Sep 2026 (passed).
funded: Independent research project of up to 3 years (4 years if part-time), including own salary.

funder: Swedish Research Council (Vetenskapsrådet) – International Postdoc
eligibility: Recent PhDs going abroad, aimed at researchers from the Swedish system†; exact PhD window set in each call (about 2 years per secondary sources†). Separate calls per area (spring call for humanities and social sciences: 9 of 115 funded in 2026).
funded: 18–36 months, mainly at a host abroad; salary and limited research costs.
amount: SEK 1,300,000/year ≈ €117,300/year; plus SEK 50,000/year for accompanying family ≈ €4,500.

funder: Forte (Swedish Research Council for Health, Working Life and Welfare) – Starting Grant
eligibility: Junior researchers up to 3 years after the doctoral degree certificate was issued; research on health, working life and welfare; via a Swedish research organisation.
funded: Two- or three-year project led by the applicant.
amount: Up to SEK 2.5m (2 years) ≈ €225,600 or SEK 3.75m (3 years) ≈ €338,500.

funder: Jan Wallander and Tom Hedelius Foundation / Tore Browaldh Foundation (Handelsbanken) – Wallander scholarship
eligibility: New PhDs from Swedish universities in economics, business administration, economic history and related fields, for an outstanding dissertation (PhD within the last year); e.g. via nomination by a department.
funded: Three years of full-time research.
amount: Most recent figure found: SEK 1,725,000 (2020 award) ≈ €155,700†; current amount not confirmed.

funder: Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation – postdoctoral scholarship programmes abroad
eligibility: Doctorate from a Swedish university no more than 2 years old at the start of the postdoc; connection to a Swedish university; invitation from a host (programmes at e.g. MIT/Broad, Stanford, NTU Singapore).
funded: Up to 2 years of postdoctoral study abroad; possible funding for up to 2 years in Sweden afterwards.
amount: MIT: about $71,000/year stipend, $7,500/year travel grant, up to $15,000/year family allowance. Amounts vary by host.

funder: Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF) – International Postdoctoral Grant
eligibility: PhD from a Danish institution, at most 3 years before the deadline (or thesis to be submitted within 12 months). At least 12 consecutive months abroad. Deadline 5 Nov 2026.
funded: Two-year independent project at a foreign host (up to 6 months at the start and/or 12 months at the end may be in Denmark); travel, bench fees.
amount: Up to DKK 1,550,000 excl. overhead ≈ €207,400; plus DKK 55,000/year per accompanying partner/child ≈ €7,400.

funder: Carlsberg Foundation – Internationalisation Fellowships
eligibility: Researchers from Denmark, Greenland or the Faroe Islands; PhD at most 3 years before the deadline. 2026 deadline was 1 Apr 2026 (annual spring call).
funded: Two- to three-year postdoc combining a stay abroad with a (shorter) period at a Danish institution.
amount: Full salary plus operating expenses of DKK 8,000/month ≈ €1,070†; abroad additionally DKK 50,000/year with partner ≈ €6,700 or DKK 100,000/year with children ≈ €13,400.

funder: Research Council of Norway – FRIPRO Researcher Project for Early Career Scientists
eligibility: Doctorate 2–7 years before submission; application via an approved Norwegian research organisation. Open-ended deadline.
funded: Researcher-led project including the applicant’s position, team and running costs; a separate mobility call combines 1–2 years abroad with 1–2 years in Norway.

funder: Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) – Postdoc.Mobility
eligibility: Revised 2026 criteria: Swiss citizens, holders of a Swiss settlement permit (C) or spouses/registered partners of Swiss citizens. Can apply up to 6 months before the PhD is completed. Remaining deadlines Feb and Aug 2027; replaced by a new postdoc scheme from 2028.
funded: Research stay abroad (24 months), optional return grant in Switzerland (3–12 months).
amount: Fellowship and travel allowance according to SNSF rate tables (depend on destination).

funder: Austrian Science Fund (FWF) – ESPRIT
eligibility: Any nationality; doctorate normally no more than 5 years before submission; Austrian host institution and a mentor. Rolling submission.
funded: 36-month independent project: own position as principal investigator plus project costs.
amount: Own salary at the FWF senior postdoc rate; project costs €45,000 flat, up to €75,000 if justified.

funder: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR) – JCJC (Jeunes chercheuses et jeunes chercheurs), part of the Generic Call
eligibility: Researchers who defended their thesis less than 10 years ago and have held their position less than 5 years (extensions for children, leave, illness). AAPG 2027 step 1 closed 13 Oct 2026.
funded: Single-team project led by the young researcher to build independence and a first team.
amount: Budget follows the annual AAPG rules; I could not confirm a ceiling on ANR’s own pages.

funder: “la Caixa” Foundation – Junior Leader postdoctoral fellowships (Incoming / Retaining)
eligibility: Any nationality; PhD 2–7 years before the deadline. Incoming: no more than 12 months in Spain/Portugal in the last 3 years; Retaining: the reverse. 2027 call restricted to STEM (life sciences, physics, chemistry, engineering, mathematics). 2027 deadline 23 Sep 2026 (passed).
funded: Three-year employment contract at a host in Spain or Portugal, plus research costs and training programme.
amount: Up to €320,100 over 3 years; minimum gross salary €47,000/year.

funder: European Economic Association – PhD Travel Grants (EEA Congress)
eligibility: PhD students presenting at the EEA Congress whose department cannot fund travel and accommodation (letter from head of department), or presenting from a low- or middle-income country. Apply by e-mail between paper acceptance and 3 May; lottery if oversubscribed. Next congress 23–27 Aug 2027.
funded: Reimbursement towards travel and accommodation after the congress; only for attendees staying more than 3 days.
amount: €400 per grant; 30 grants.

funder: Weiss Fund for Research in Development Economics (University of Chicago)
eligibility: Students and faculty at any university (non-UChicago applicants go through their own grants office); junior faculty via self-nomination. Projects must focus on countries, regions or populations with GDP per capita below $13,750 (preference below $6,875). Rolling deadlines for requests under $25,000: 1 Nov 2026, 1 Feb 2027, 1 May 2027; larger requests in spring/fall calls.
funded: Research grants plus separate travel and piloting grants: data collection, data purchase, field travel, materials, research assistance. No tuition, salaries, stipends or overhead.
amount: PhD students typically up to $50,000 ($75,000 exceptionally); junior and senior faculty up to $100,000 ($150,000). Travel grants up to $15,000; pilots up to $25,000.

funder: PEDL (CEPR/FCDO) – Special Exploratory Research Grants for PhD students
eligibility: All investigators must be current PhD students (any university), with a supervisor’s letter. Projects in low-income countries and FCDO-focus lower-middle-income countries (Myanmar and Palestine currently excluded; India and Indonesia lower priority). 8th call closed 16 Aug 2026; PEDL also runs calls for researchers based in low-income countries.
funded: Private-sector development research: research assistance, data collection, new surveys; teaching buy-out if needed.

funder: STEG (CEPR/FCDO) – PhD Research Grants
eligibility: Current PhD students (supervisor letter); research on low- and middle-income countries with policy relevance for low-income countries, especially sub-Saharan Africa; India-only projects ineligible. 10th call closed 15 Sep 2026.
funded: Research assistance, data collection/purchase, travel to field sites, and stipends that buy out teaching/admin duties.
amount: Up to £15,000 (stipend part capped at £12,000 for programmes in high-income countries).

funder: Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) – competitive research funds
eligibility: Thematic initiatives (e.g. peace and recovery, displaced livelihoods, consumer protection, citizen security) open to applicants from any institution with sufficient expertise. No call open as of October 2026; calls recur.
funded: Exploratory/pilot work and full randomised evaluations in low- and middle-income countries.
amount: Varies by initiative; not stated on the overview page.

funder: dggö (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Gesundheitsökonomie) – Tagungsfonds for young scientists
eligibility: dggö members at a university in Germany, Austria or Switzerland (or external doctorate); pay no higher than TV-L 14 / W1; last qualification (master’s, doctorate or junior professorship) at most 6 years ago. Talk must be formally accepted; one award per year. Deadlines 30 Apr and 30 Oct.
funded: Presenting at a prestigious international conference.
amount: Up to €500.

funder: DAAD – Kongressreisenprogramm (and Vortragsreisenprogramm)
eligibility: Currently closed: DAAD states that applications are not possible at present. When open: doctoral candidates enrolled at a German university and researchers at German institutions living in Germany; active participation (talk/poster) abroad; once per calendar year during the PhD and the first 5 years after. Documents due 120 days before the event.
funded: In-person: travel flat rate by distance, daily allowance, material-cost flat rate. Online: registration, membership (1 year) and abstract fees.
amount: Material-cost flat rate €300; travel and daily rates by destination (DAAD rate tables).

funder: Joachim Herz Stiftung – Add-on Fellowships for Interdisciplinary Science and Transfer
eligibility: Advanced PhD candidates, postdocs (PhD at most 5 years ago, 6 with children/care) and junior professors without tenure track, integrated in the German science system; economics, business administration, life sciences or materials science, with an interdisciplinary topic. Not for those already leading a DFG/BMFTR/EU-funded project. Annual call; next expected spring 2027.
funded: Personal research budget for 2 years and 3 months: data collection/acquisition, student assistants, hardware/software, conference fees and travel, training, own workshops. Does not cover living costs.
amount: Up to €15,000, plus up to €3,000 for childcare/care/disability-related costs.

funder: Stiftung Deutsch-Amerikanische Wissenschaftsbeziehungen (SDAW, Stifterverband)
eligibility: Doctoral candidates and postdocs of all disciplines incl. economics, with research on transatlantic relations or related political/social questions. Active participation only (talk or poster). Deadlines 30 Apr and 30 Sep†.
funded: Registration, travel and accommodation for international conferences.

funder: Fritz Thyssen Stiftung – Reisebeihilfen (travel subsidies)
eligibility: Researchers who already hold a doctorate; application via a university or non-profit research institution; project must link to German research and to the Foundation’s areas (incl. “State, Economy and Society”). No deadline.
funded: Research travel tied to a project (e.g. archive or data visits). Conference and lecture travel is not funded.
amount: Travel costs plus a daily allowance at the Foundation’s country rates.

funder: Royal Economic Society – Conference grants
eligibility: RES members who are PhD students or early-career economists presenting an economics paper at a research or teaching conference; head-of-department statement. The most recent RES pages I could read are from 2021 (and 2015 for rounds), so check current rules.
funded: Conference fees, travel and/or accommodation.
amount: Up to £500.

funder: Scottish Economic Society – Small Grants
eligibility: Society members for at least 2 years. PhD Student Conference Support: PhD students (proof that internal funding was sought). Early Career Researcher Support: within 5 years of the PhD. Deadlines end of September, January and April.
funded: PhD students: fees, travel, accommodation to present at a research conference (not the SES conference). ECRs: a small piece of research (co-funding encouraged).
amount: PhD students up to £750; ECRs up to £2,000.

funder: Economic History Society – Research Fund for Graduate Students
eligibility: EHS members who are master’s or PhD students at UK institutions, working on economic and/or social history. Supervisor statement. Deadlines 1 May and 1 Nov.
funded: Gathering data and source material, research travel and accommodation, data-input costs. Not conference attendance, equipment or subsistence.
amount: Normally up to £1,000.

funder: British Academy / Leverhulme – Small Research Grants
eligibility: Postdoctoral level or equivalent (current PhD students not eligible); ordinarily resident in the UK; humanities and social sciences. Next deadline 4 Nov 2026 (results by 16 Apr 2027).
funded: Research expenses over up to 24 months: datasets and other consumables, survey-provider payments to participants, research travel incl. conference dissemination. No books, hardware or salary.

funder: Jan Wallander and Tom Hedelius Foundation – Hedelius scholarship for doctoral studies abroad
eligibility: Doctoral students of any nationality enrolled at a Swedish university, in economics, business administration, economic history, economic geography or econometrics†. Autumn round 10 Aug–15 Sep.
funded: Extra costs of a research stay abroad (usually up to 6 months at a leading university): travel, insurance. Not ordinary living costs.
amount: Varies by destination and length; in 2025, 30 awards totalling SEK 5.2m (average ≈ €15,600)†.

funder: Russell Sage Foundation – Dissertation Research Grants
eligibility: Doctoral students with dissertations in RSF’s priority areas (behavioural science and decision making, future of work, immigration, inequality); research must relate to social and living conditions in the U.S.
funded: Dissertation research projects (RSF also runs a joint dissertation programme with the Upjohn Institute on employment topics).
amount: Amount not confirmed on RSF’s site; a Rutgers listing for RSF’s small awards in behavioural economics gives $7,500†.

funder: Washington Center for Equitable Growth – Early career grants
eligibility: PI must be at a U.S. institution: doctoral students at the dissertation stage, or scholars with a PhD from the last 8 years (postdocs included; tenured researchers excluded). International students at U.S. universities eligible. Annual request for proposals.
funded: Policy-relevant research on inequality and growth (competition, families, labour, mobility, tax/macro): salary, research assistance, data purchase, experiments, conference costs. No overhead.
amount: Doctoral students $15,000 (1 year); early-career scholars $30,000 (1–2 years).

funder: W.E. Upjohn Institute – Early Career Research Awards
eligibility: Within 6 years of the PhD; economics, sociology, public policy, political science and related fields. 2026 deadline was 23 Jan 2026; 2027 details to be announced.
funded: Research on employment and public workforce policy, resulting in an Upjohn working paper and a policy brief.

funder: Spencer Foundation – Small Research Grants on Education
eligibility: PI and co-PIs must hold a doctorate (PhD students can be team members only); international applicants eligible; grant administered by a non-profit or public institution. Two rounds per year (one deadline was 15 Apr 2026)†.
funded: Education research projects of 1–5 years.

funder: SSHRC – Insight Development Grants
eligibility: Researchers affiliated with an eligible Canadian institution (postdocs and PhD graduates can apply if they hold an eligible affiliation by the start; enrolled students cannot); at least 50% of funds reserved for emerging scholars. Annual competition with an early-February deadline.
funded: Short-term research in its early stages; eligible costs per SSHRC rules.

funder: JSPS KAKENHI – Grant-in-Aid for Early-Career Scientists
eligibility: Researchers at an eligible Japanese institution with a doctorate obtained within the last 8 years (or under 39)†.
funded: Researcher-led project of 2–4 years.
